title: Everybody Goes Out Except Me
trend: TikTok 'In this town everybody goes out partying except me' (Virlo weekly list, week of Nov 16 2026, 417 posts, New; Virlo November list updated Nov 23 2026, US) + the Saturday-before-Thanksgiving going-out weekend — self-pity lament skit: homebody Desmond in a blanket narrates that the whole town goes out except him while his phone reads everyone's party posts; he turns down every invite with worse excuses (the soup, the plant, his good socks); twist: his sister Tasha knocks — every party post was staged around his building, the whole town is in the hallway because the party came to him; button: everybody takes their shoes off and goes home at nine
youtube_title: In this town everybody goes out on Saturday night. Except me. 🛋️
description:
Saturday night. The whole town is out. Desmond is in a blanket with soup and a plant, and his phone will not stop showing him every party. Then somebody knocks.

#cartoon #animation #funny #comedy #homebody #shorts
tiktok_caption: in this town everybody goes out except me 🛋️ #cartoon #animation #funny #homebody

lines.text: In this town, everybody goes out on Saturday night. Except me.
Hello. I am his phone. He has not left this couch since Tuesday.
That is not true. I went to the mailbox. In my socks.
It was raining. He came back with one sock.
Look at this. Everybody is out. Everybody is happy.
Marcus is at the bowling place. Twelve people. Matching shirts.
Matching shirts. Nobody asked me about a shirt.
They asked you four times. You said you were busy.
I was busy. I had soup.
He had soup for three hours.
It was a big soup.
Now Kim is at the rooftop place. There is a band. There are little lights.
Little lights. I have a little light. It is in the fridge.
He opens the fridge just to feel something.
Do not tell people that.
New message. Come out tonight. We miss you. Bring nothing.
Bring nothing. That is suspicious. What are they hiding?
He is typing. He is deleting. He is typing again.
Sorry. I cannot. My plant needs me.
The plant is plastic. He bought it so it would not need him.
Okay, fine. Maybe I will go out. A little bit.
He put on one nice shoe. Then he sat down again.
The other shoe is under the couch. The couch does not want me to leave.
He is negotiating with furniture.
Everyone is out there living. And I am in here. With a blanket that has sleeves.
The blanket is very nice. I will give him that.
Show me one more post. Just one. I like to suffer.
Tasha is at a big party. She says, best night ever. She is in a hallway.
A hallway party. That is not even a place.
That hallway looks a lot like your hallway.
All hallways look the same. That is why they are hallways.
That doormat says go away. You have that doormat.
Lots of people have that doormat. It is a very popular doormat.
Marcus just posted again. He is also in the hallway now.
Why is the bowling team in a hallway?
Somebody is knocking.
Nobody knock. I am not home. I am out partying.
Desmond. I can hear you. I can see your blanket through the little hole.
Tasha? Why are you here? You are at a big party.
I am at a big party. It is in your hallway. It has been there for an hour.
The bowling place. The rooftop. The little lights.
All fake. Marcus took that bowling picture by your mailbox. The lights are from my car.
I knew. I have known since Wednesday. I am a very good phone.
You knew? You let me suffer?
You asked me to show you one more post. You like to suffer.
In this town, everybody goes out. Except you. So the town came in.
How many people are in my hallway?
Twenty two. And a dog. And the lady from downstairs with her famous dip.
The dip lady is here? Okay. Okay. You can come in.
Bring nothing, we said. Because we brought everything.
Wait. Rules. Everybody takes their shoes off.
He found both shoes for this. Incredible.
And everybody goes home at nine.
It is nine fifteen.
Then everybody goes home at ten.
In this town, everybody goes out. And then everybody comes to Desmond.
